title: Spec 112 §15A.1 (gap): focusa uninstall subcommand in Rust. Mirror of focusa install: stop daemon, remove service unit, remove binaries, remove symlinks, remove license.json, rollback on failure. Acceptance: `focusa uninstall --dry-run --keep-license` parses; restores prior state if anything fails. Evidence: crates/focusa-cli/src/commands/install.rs (or new uninstall.rs) ; crates/focusa-cli/src/main.rs
description:
Implements `focusa uninstall` Rust subcommand. Mirrors `focusa install` per Spec 112 §15A.1.

SCOPE (what gets removed in default mode, no flags):
  1. Stop daemon via POST /v1/daemon/stop (idempotent — succeeds if already stopped)
  2. Remove systemd user unit (Linux) OR launchd LaunchAgent (macOS) OR sc.exe (Windows)
  3. Remove symlinks created by install:
     - ~/.local/bin/focusa
     - ~/.local/bin/focusa-daemon (if present)
     - ~/.local/bin/focusa-tui (if present)
     - /usr/local/bin/focusa (if writeable)
  4. Remove ~/.focusa/ directory (bin, share, state, install metadata)
  5. Remove ~/.config/focusa/license.json (unless --keep-license)
  6. Revert PATH modifications in:
     - ~/.bashrc (remove the line that exports PATH=...\/root/.local/bin...)
     - ~/.zshrc (same)
     - ~/.config/fish/config.fish (same)
     - Powershell profile (Windows)

FLAGS:
  --target=<auto|linux|darwin|windows-x64|windows-arm64>    mirror of install
  --dry-run              show plan + commands without executing
  --keep-license         don't delete ~/.config/focusa/license.json
  --keep-data            don't delete ~/.focusa/ (only remove service + symlinks + PATH)
  --keep-path-modifications    don't edit rc files
  --purge                full nuclear option (also removes skill files in ~/.pi/skills)
  --json                 machine-readable output

ACCEPTANCE (must all pass for bead close):
  - [ ] `focusa uninstall --dry-run` prints structured plan in both human and --json forms
  - [ ] `focusa uninstall` (no flags) removes service, symlinks, ~/.focusa/, license.json, and reverts rc files
  - [ ] `focusa uninstall --keep-license` preserves ~/.config/focusa/license.json
  - [ ] `focusa uninstall --keep-data` preserves ~/.focusa/ but removes service + symlinks + rc
  - [ ] `focusa uninstall --keep-path-modifications` preserves rc files
  - [ ] If any step fails, the prior steps are NOT rolled back unless --atomicity flag is set
  - [ ] On macOS, launchctl bootout before removing LaunchAgent
  - [ ] On Linux, systemctl --user disable --now before removing unit
  - [ ] On Windows, sc.exe delete before removing unit
  - [ ] Idempotent: re-running on an already-uninstalled host returns ok with recovery_hint
  - [ ] Static guard test verifies all flags + main.rs dispatch + module wiring

EVIDENCE CITATIONS (deliverable file paths):
  - crates/focusa-cli/src/commands/uninstall.rs (new — install.rs mirror)
  - crates/focusa-cli/src/commands/mod.rs (pub mod uninstall)
  - crates/focusa-cli/src/main.rs (Commands::Uninstall dispatch)
  - crates/focusa-cli/src/commands/service.rs (extend ServiceManager with Uninstall variant)
  - tests/spec_focusa_112_uninstall_cmd_static_test.sh (new)

ATOMICITY: Default mode is best-effort (no rollback). Add --atomicity flag in a follow-up bead (focusa-112-atomicity already covers rollback patterns we can mirror).
notes:
Spec 112 §15A.1 gap: every install needs an uninstall. The shell installer has --uninstall mode (scripts/install-focusa.sh line 16) but the new Rust install orchestrator has no mirror. This bead closes the install/uninstall lifecycle for the 24h-market cut.

WORK BREAKDOWN (sequential):
  1. Extend ServiceManager enum with Uninstall variant in service.rs (~30 min)
  2. Implement run_uninstall_systemd_user + run_uninstall_launchd_user (~30 min)
  3. Create crates/focusa-cli/src/commands/uninstall.rs with full Args/Report/Plan structs and run() (~1.0h)
  4. Wire into main.rs Commands::Uninstall dispatch (~15 min)
  5. Static guard + 4 unit tests (~30 min)

TRANSCRIPT CONTEXT: 2026-07-03 Cursor evaluator never tested uninstall, but the spec 112 §0 'CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: No Deferrals for Compatible Systems' applies symmetrically — every install must have a clean uninstall path. Without this, every 'try it once' user becomes permanent system baggage.

UninstallArgs exposes --target/--dry-run/--keep-license/--keep-data/--keep-path-modifications/--purge/--yes/--json. service::uninstall_service() per-platform dispatcher (launchctl bootout macOS, systemctl --user disable Linux, sc.exe Windows). title: Fix contradictory unbound-project onboarding and init guidance
description:
Summary: First-run project binding is contradictory and unnecessarily rough. The Pi unbound-project nag tells operators to run `focusa about` and `focusa init`, but `focusa about` only prints a generic product primer, while the recommended `focusa init` immediately warns that it is deprecated and names two ambiguous replacements (`focusa project new / focusa setup init`). In degraded mode, the Utility Card also requests an operator-defined trajectory before the project marker exists, obscuring the prerequisite project-binding action.

Observed reproduction (Focusa 0.9.120-dev, macOS):
1. Start Pi in an existing Git repository without `.focusa-project.json`.
2. Receive the unbound-project nag recommending `focusa about`, `focusa init`, or remote onboarding.
3. Run `focusa about`; it does not inspect or explain current project binding.
4. Run `focusa init --help`; help calls it “Minimal low-risk project bootstrap”.
5. Run `focusa init --quickstart --project-root <repo> --json`; it succeeds but first emits `Deprecated alias. Use: focusa project new / focusa setup init`.
6. Utility Card reports missing HLT/action authority and asks for trajectory definition even though binding is the immediate prerequisite.

Files/surfaces to inspect:
- `apps/pi-extension/src/session.ts` (unbound-project nag)
- `crates/focusa-cli/src/main.rs` and `crates/focusa-cli/src/commands/help.rs` (alias warning)
- `crates/focusa-cli/src/commands/init.rs`, `setup.rs`, and `project.rs` (canonical command ownership)
- `docs/current/CLI_REFERENCE_CURRENT.md`, README/onboarding walkthroughs, and static/e2e tests
- Utility Card bootstrap routing for unbound projects

Implementation direction:
1. Choose one canonical command for binding an existing repository and use it everywhere.
2. Distinguish “bind this existing repo” from “create a new project”; do not present both as interchangeable replacements.
3. Make the unbound nag’s first command perform or clearly preview binding; replace generic `focusa about` guidance with a project-aware status command if needed.
4. Ensure degraded Utility Cards prioritize marker initialization before HLT/Workpoint requests.
5. Add a clean-repo first-run regression test covering nag → command → marker verification with no contradictory deprecation warning.

Related prior work: `focusa-gh-7-pi-unbound-nag` added the current nag and is closed; this ticket captures the observed end-to-end UX regression after command hierarchy changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- A new operator in an existing unbound Git repo receives one exact, copy-pasteable canonical binding command.
- The recommended command does not warn that it is deprecated and does not offer multiple ambiguous replacements.
- Binding success verifies the marker path/project identity and gives the next single action.
- HLT/Workpoint guidance appears after project binding, not before it.
- Docs, Pi nag, CLI help, TUI/walkthroughs, and regression tests agree on the same command and terminology.
close_reason: Completed: focusa init --quickstart is the canonical existing-repository binding path with no deprecation warning; Pi nag, Utility Card, CLI reference, and regression tests now enforce binding-first marker verification.

title: GitHub #109 — P0 REGRESSION: foreign TRAJECTORY_CONTEXT contaminates scoped Pi tool output
description:
Cross-project state bleed observed in a philoveracity-launch-pages Pi session:

1. focusa_predict_recent returned predictions scoped to project=/home/planmarr/plan-the-marriage continuity=focusa-cont-plan-the-marriage-... while the active session project_root was /home/focusadev/philoveracity-launch-pages. The tool has NO project_root parameter and returns globally most-recent predictions, ignoring the active project.

2. focusa_trajectory_view (and TRAJECTORY_CONTEXT prefix injected into handle ECS blocks) returned HLT=Run PlanTheMarriage as a profitable course business... on calls intended for the philoveracity-launch-pages scope. Daemon appears to key trajectory/prediction reads by continuity_id / session fingerprint, NOT by project_root.

Repro: In a Pi session bound to project_root=/home/focusadev/philoveracity-launch-pages, call focusa_predict_recent (no project_root param) — returns another projects predictions. Call focusa_trajectory_view — may return another projects HLT via trajectory handle context.

Expected: focusa_predict_recent, focusa_trajectory_view, and handle ECS TRAJECTORY_CONTEXT rehydration MUST filter by the same project_root used to bootstrap the session. No cross-project HLT/prediction/metacog bleed.

Fix direction: Add project_root parameter to focusa_predict_recent (and any read that lacks one); enforce active project_root as the filter key for trajectory handle rehydration; do not fall back to most-recent-across-projects when continuity_id is unbound.

Related: focusa-l38o (trajectory wrapper cache bleed), focusa-oh7t (focusa_decide rejected as attentive).
acceptance_criteria:
P0 closure requires end-to-end typed-scope isolation:
1. Every prompt-visible TRAJECTORY_CONTEXT/ECS augmentation keys by explicit verified project_root + continuity_id + working subpath, never global-most-recent state.
2. Generic read/bash/tool outputs for project A cannot inject HLT/MLG/STG/predictions from project B.
3. No foreign fallback occurs when scope is missing, stale, broad /root, or temporarily switched for issue filing; fail closed with bounded recovery.
4. Behavioral tests use at least two projects with distinct trajectories and identical/rotated continuity patterns across read, bash, prediction, trajectory, compaction, and rehydrate surfaces.
5. Raw tool payload and rendered augmentation are independently tested so post-execution injection cannot evade route tests.
6. Wire Pitch reproduction (canonical Workpoint + read of PHP files) returns Wire Pitch context or no augmentation, never Focusa locked-release context.
7. Release evidence identifies the deployed fix commit/version and proves no regression across Pi restart/compaction/project switch.
notes: P0 acceptance progress 2026-07-31: candidate commits 9626ac53/f8a7cbf0/5dafaa34/ed5340ea plus ESI-018 prove exact project+continuity isolation, migration, restart/reconnect, and proposal replay. Dedicated Pi cross-project suite passes 7/7; commit added explicit read/bash foreign-project and rotated-continuity rejection. Full Pi suite passed. Workset execution audit now verified with unique frontier focusa-gkwt. Mac read-only inventory: MacBook-Pro.lan user vsmith, Pi 0.83.0, Focusa 0.9.138, managed extension present. Remaining: release/version gates and installed Mac update/restart/compaction/project-switch proof; do not downgrade installed 0.9.141 VPS daemon with 0.9.137-dev candidate.
close_reason: Completed: exact project+continuity isolation is proven across ECS raw/rendered augmentation, read/bash, predictions, trajectory, session restore, migration, daemon restart/reconnect, and fail-closed broad roots; candidate version/fix lineage and final Mac update boundary are recorded in ESI-018.

title: P0: Replace unbounded PTY capture with Pi semantic event integration
description:
## Confirmed defect

`focusa wrap -- pi` currently treats interactive TUI mode as a raw terminal-recording problem:

- `crates/focusa-cli/src/commands/wrap.rs:276-308` launches `script -q -c ... -a /tmp/focusa-session-*.txt` with no byte/time bound, rotation, redaction, or backpressure.
- `wrap.rs:310-318` reads the entire recording into one Rust `String` only after Pi exits, then removes the file.
- `wrap.rs:510-545` parses the raw PTY after exit and submits the complete terminal transcript as `assistant_output` to `/v1/turn/complete`.
- Cleanup does not occur during a long-running session and is not crash/signal safe.
- The only three local unit tests cover semantic exit classification; there are zero recording-size/lifecycle tests.

## Production evidence

Confidence: **99.5%**.

Running binary/process chain:

```text
focusa wrap -- pi
  -> script -q -c pi -a /tmp/focusa-session-*.txt
    -> pi
```

Observed in one live session:

- raw PTY recording: `1,074,626,560` bytes;
- canonical Pi semantic JSONL: `5,792,804` bytes;
- total amplification: about `185x`;
- same two-second interval: raw `+2,674,688` bytes vs semantic JSONL `+9,216` bytes (about `290x`);
- bounded 200-frame mock TUI: 8,203-byte final semantic state produced a 1,642,176-byte typescript (`200.2x`);
- a 4 MiB live sample contained 165,002 CSI sequences and compressed to 15.37%, confirming repaint/control-stream amplification rather than equivalent semantic content.

Operational consequences:

1. unbounded `/tmp` disk consumption during long interactive sessions;
2. whole-file heap allocation/OOM risk when the harness exits;
3. oversized `/v1/turn/complete` payloads and duplicate context/token pressure;
4. raw terminal data may include sensitive input/output that should not be persisted or uploaded as an assistant message;
5. stale files can survive abnormal wrapper termination.

## Pi-native foundation (do not degrade capability)

Build on Pi's documented semantic surfaces instead of screen scraping:

1. **Interactive Pi — primary:** the existing Focusa Pi extension subscribes to typed lifecycle events (`session_start`, `before_agent_start`, `agent_start`, `message_start/update/end`, `tool_execution_start/update/end`, `agent_end`, compaction/tree events, `session_shutdown`). Use `ctx.sessionManager` for canonical entries, branch state, and session-file identity.
2. **Node/TypeScript embedding:** Pi documentation recommends using `AgentSession` directly rather than spawning a subprocess; subscribe to typed session events.
3. **Non-Node subprocess/headless:** use `pi --mode rpc`, whose stdout is JSONL semantic events with correlated message/tool IDs; use JSON mode where one-way event output is sufficient.
4. **Recovery/replay:** use Pi's append-only, tree-structured session JSONL as the durable semantic source, preserving branching, compaction, custom entries, usage, and tool results.
5. **Optional forensic PTY capture only:** disabled by default; if explicitly enabled, use a redacted bounded ring/spool and externalize it to ECS as an artifact handle. Never inline it as `assistant_output`.

This is strictly richer than the current approach: it preserves message IDs, tool-call correlation, deltas, usage, branch/compaction lineage, and graceful shutdown while eliminating ANSI repaint noise.

Pi documentation anchors:

- `docs/session-format.md:3-32` — canonical tree-structured JSONL and `SessionManager` types;
- `docs/extensions.md` — typed session/agent/message/tool lifecycle events and `ctx.sessionManager`;
- `docs/sdk.md` — `AgentSession` and typed event subscription;
- `docs/rpc.md` — prefer `AgentSession` for Node embeddings; RPC JSONL for subprocess integration;
- `docs/json.md` — semantic JSON event output;
- Focusa `docs/44-pi-focusa-integration-spec.md:46` — handles over blobs; large artifacts externalized, never inlined by default.

## Required design

### Semantic event bridge

- Define a versioned `PiSemanticEventEnvelope` containing project/workstream scope, Pi session ID, Focusa turn ID, event type, message ID/toolCallId, parent/branch refs, timestamps, usage, bounded inline content, and artifact handles.
- Make event ingestion idempotent by `(session_id, event_type, message_id/toolCallId, sequence)`.
- Stream/store final semantic messages and tool outcomes incrementally; do not wait for session shutdown.
- Apply content redaction and output-firewall rules before persistence.
- Externalize oversized tool/message bodies to ECS and retain bounded handles.
- Use a bounded offline spool with backpressure when the daemon is unavailable.

### Wrapper behavior

- Preserve `focusa wrap -- pi` UX and Focusa environment/context injection.
- For interactive Pi, ensure/load the Focusa extension and wait on the child process without `script` recording.
- Derive turn completion from semantic events/session state, not terminal output.
- Keep non-Pi harness adapters explicit; do not silently apply Pi assumptions globally.

### Optional diagnostics

- Raw PTY capture default: off.
- Explicit opt-in maximum: 8 MiB ring buffer per session unless a stricter configured budget applies.
- Redact before storage; store as ECS artifact, return only a handle.
- Cleanup on normal exit, signal, crash recovery, and startup scavenging; never remove a file held by a live process.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A simulated 10,000-redraw interactive Pi run produces no unbounded transcript file; raw diagnostic storage remains at or below the configured cap.
2. Long-running sessions emit semantic turn/message/tool evidence incrementally and preserve current TUI behavior.
3. `assistant_output` contains semantic assistant content/handles, never a raw ANSI transcript.
4. Wrapper exit cannot allocate memory proportional to total session duration/output.
5. Daemon-offline operation remains bounded and recoverable without blocking Pi.
6. Branch, resume, compaction, steering, tool updates, usage, and session shutdown have conformance tests.
7. Secret/redaction tests prove terminal/user/tool secrets are not copied into Focusa payloads or artifacts.
8. Crash/signal/startup tests prove stale `/tmp/focusa-session-*` cleanup is safe and auditable.
9. Migration includes a governed dry-run/receipt path for existing stale recordings.
10. A regression test reproduces the current 200x repaint amplification and proves the new semantic path remains bounded.

title: Post-lock: broad-cwd project binding and Workpoint lease bootstrap deadlock
description: Post-scope-lock follow-up to GitHub #44. Explicit verified child project_root must outrank stale /root persisted scope, and first Workpoint checkpoint must not deadlock on Work Loop writer lease.
acceptance_criteria:
Regression closure requires behavioral coverage and runtime proof:
1. Given verified child project root + canonical project-bound Workpoint + active_writer=none, work_loop_control(on) acquires a scoped writer or returns one executable non-circular recovery.
2. work_loop_checkpoint and work_loop_context become usable after bootstrap; no writer-before-writer deadlock.
3. Preflight and mutation resolve identical project_root, continuity_id, route, and writer identity.
4. No expected=unknown packet=unknown response when canonical Workpoint scope exists.
5. Broad /root session cwd cannot override explicit verified child project scope.
6. Positive and negative behavioral tests cover stale/foreign writer, no writer, and scope mismatch.
7. Release evidence identifies deployed commit/version and proves the original 99c3c258 behavior remains present.
notes: Release-blocking resume crash fixed: removed delayed ctx.ui use after agent_end; receptionist idle scheduler catches stale ctx after session replacement/reload; Pi shim now bypasses legacy wrapper for all Pi invocations (new/-c/-r/print/json/rpc). Exact tmux 'pi -c' proof stayed alive 25s with no uncaughtException, stale ctx, wrapper DEBUG, extension failure, or skill collision.

title: P0: Portable Mac pairing room architecture and fallback UX
description: Real Mac v0.9.33 test exposed portability gaps. First-run Mac QR is a focusa-connect-v1 JSON handoff offer; generic phone camera shows raw JSON. Intended flow requires operator to open a VPS/public Focusa Connect Page and scan the Mac QR there, but current VPS room resolved to local-only http://127.0.0.1:8787/connect/... and public hostname probe 404s. Mac callback listener is ready at LAN http://192.168.1.59:<port>/..., causing expected macOS incoming-network prompt. The architecture must be fully portable to any VPS or local machine: discover/require reachable server_url, support local LAN/Tailscale/tunnel/public URL, expose manual completion payload fallback, and make UX explain why phone camera raw JSON is not success.
acceptance_criteria: 1. focusa pair refuses/clearly warns when only 127.0.0.1 room is available for cross-device pairing and prints exact public/tunnel/local alternatives. 2. UI copy explains: generic phone camera showing JSON is expected; open Focusa Connect Page first. 4. Version mismatch between CLI and daemon is repaired or blocked with exact command. 5. Docs/tests cover VPS public URL, local-only, LAN, and Tailscale/tunnel pairing modes. Evidence citations required before close.

title: P0: Controller-daemon multiplexing for remote projects and worktrees
description:
## Problem
Focusa's machine-readable identity accepts `remote_host`, `remote_user`, `remote_port`, repo, workspace, and deploy-root hints, and the Pi extension persists those hints in the project-switch ledger. However, canonical bootstrap/Genesis/Workpoint authority still assumes `project_root` exists on the daemon host. A controller daemon cannot canonically manage an SSH/VPS checkout or multiple remote worktrees without either installing another daemon remotely or fabricating a local checkout.

This violates the intended one-developer/team, one-controller-daemon multiplexing model and reproduces PTM: `/home/planmarr/plan-the-marriage` is verified remotely and its HLT persists, while `focusa_project_bootstrap` is local-only and the first Workpoint enters a writer-lease cycle (`checkpoint requires lease; lease requires checkpoint`).

## Existing coverage and false closure
- `docs/issues/remote-project-marker-bug.md` correctly documents no remote write capability and names PTM.
- Closed `focusa-gh-5-remote-marker` claims remote onboarding complete.
- `crates/focusa-cli/src/commands/onboard.rs::ensure_project_marker()` writes only `project_root.join(".focusa-project.json")`; it has no SSH transport.
- `focusa onboard --remote` means "record this git URL in a marker at a locally accessible project root," not "bind a remote checkout."
- `tests/spec_focusa_gh5_remote_marker_static_test.sh` and onboarding runtime tests only prove local marker creation.
- `crates/focusa-api/src/routes/project.rs::discover_identity()` detects `remote_nonlocal` but never writes remotely or creates controller-side canonical bootstrap authority.
- Project-scope skill/compact utility guidance has no executable remote-multiplex branch; utility-card scope can remain stale after switching between PTM and Focusa.

## Required architecture
Implement a controller-owned `RemoteWorkspaceBinding` (name may vary) that lets one Focusa daemon multiplex many local projects, SSH/VPS projects, repositories, worktrees, and team sessions without a daemon on each target host.

Typed authority must include at least:
- controller/daemon identity
- project_id + repo_remote
- transport kind and verified remote host/user/port (or agent-kb host reference)
- canonical remote root/deploy root
- working_subpath/worktree identity
- continuity_id + session/team principal
- freshness, verification evidence, binding status, and revocation state

The controller-side binding is canonical. A remote `.focusa-project.json` is an optional mirror/compatibility artifact, not a prerequisite. Remote writes require explicit approval and governed SSH/agent-kb transport; credentials remain secret references and are never persisted in markers, logs, Workpoints, or ledgers.

Bootstrap, Trajectory, Genesis, Workpoint, Evidence, writer leases, session transfer, compact workbook/utility card, and recovery must all resolve through this binding. Writer ownership must be scoped by project + continuity + working subpath, allowing safe concurrent projects/worktrees without cross-scope leakage.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A remote root absent from the daemon filesystem can be bound using verified remote evidence with no remote Focusa daemon.
2. Full Bootstrap creates canonical HLT, Trajectory, first Workpoint, evidence scope, and writer lease through the controller binding.
3. Missing remote marker does not block canonical operation; optional approved marker mirroring is idempotent and conflict-safe.
4. One daemon simultaneously manages at least two remote projects and two worktrees/working subpaths per project with isolated state.
5. Two developer/team sessions can operate concurrently; writer leases and mutations cannot cross project/continuity/subpath boundaries.
6. Daemon/Pi restart restores exact bindings and Workpoints without falling back to `/root`, stale utility cards, or transcript inference.
7. Project switching immediately updates compact workbook, utility card, preload, machine-readable schemas, skills, and next-tool guidance.
8. Scope mismatch fails closed with a repair action that preserves the verified remote binding; no checkpoint/lease circular dependency.
9. Local projects and existing markers remain backward compatible.
10. Security tests prove host verification, approval gates, revocation, secret-pointer-only persistence, and no remote installation requirement.
11. Integration fixture proves PTM-style topology end-to-end: controller daemon + SSH client checkout + live deploy root + canonical resume after restart.
12. Replace/close stale `docs/issues/remote-project-marker-bug.md` with current architecture and add conformance/proof commands.

## Proof requirements
- Unit tests for binding identity, authority, persistence, revocation, and scope isolation.
- Runtime integration tests using disposable SSH targets/worktrees, not static source grep alone.
- Restart/resume and concurrent-team tests.
- Tool-schema/CLI/REST/MCP parity proof.
- Compact workbook and skill golden tests for remote project switching.
- PTM-compatible acceptance receipt showing Full Bootstrap and canonical Workpoint without installing Focusa remotely.

title: Troubleshoot Pi extension cross-session contamination
description: Reported Pi extension cross-session contamination: sessions can display or carry state from another Pi session/root Workpoint. Audit and patch session isolation boundaries.
notes:
Investigating reported Pi extension cross-session contamination after Utility Card root-session leakage fix. Scope: session_start/session_switch/fork/compaction state reset, singleton S caches, persisted session entries, Workpoint packet stamping, Focus Slice and Utility Card injection.
Root cause confirmed for Pi Task/title cross-session leak: session_start/session_switch restored focusa-state entry frameTitle/frameGoal/currentAsk before checking entry.data.sessionId, and singleton S did not have one comprehensive session-scope reset. Implemented resetPiSessionScopedState and require entry.data.sessionId === current eventSessionId before any persisted restore. Runtime proof seeds fake "Pi Task: SPEC96 FROM OTHER SESSION" and asserts reset/Utility Card do not leak it. Tests: tsc, spec96_utility_card_session_isolation_static_test, spec96_broad_root_scope_isolation_static_test.
close_reason: Completed: fixed Pi extension cross-session contamination by resetting session-scoped singleton state and requiring persisted entry sessionId match before restoring Pi Task/title/currentAsk. code: apps/pi-extension/src/state.ts:203. code: apps/pi-extension/src/session.ts:218. code: tests/utility_card_session_isolation_test.mts:54. spec section §12.1. Evidence citations: tests/spec96_utility_card_session_isolation_static_test.sh; tests/spec96_broad_root_scope_isolation_static_test.sh; apps/pi-extension tsc --noEmit; validate-focusa-tool-contracts 58/58.

title: Skill: focusa-roadmap-to-workpoint — scope discovery, audited execution graph, and Trajectory-to-Workpoint derivation
description:
PROBLEM
Agents lack one bounded, reusable workflow for the complete pre-implementation reasoning chain: verify project scope; discover live authority/current state; close decisions; map blockers/risks; design implementation order; materialize provider-neutral tasks and dependencies; prepare exact point-of-need contracts; audit graph correctness; derive MLG → STG → Waypoint → current Workpoint; and expose the first authorized ready frontier. Existing Project Genesis, Mission Canvas, Spec Implementation, Trajectory, and Workpoint capabilities own adjacent primitives but no skill composes the end-to-end sequence.

PROPOSED SKILL
Name: focusa-roadmap-to-workpoint
Descriptor: Scope-to-Execution-Graph and Trajectory Planning Skill
Authority: orchestration only. It must compose existing canonical tools/providers and never create a parallel task, Trajectory, Workpoint, evidence, or authorization authority.

TRIGGER EXAMPLES
- thoroughly plan the roadmap before implementation
- map every implementation task, dependency, milestone, and critical path
- prepare dependencies at the point needed
- infer the Trajectory ladder from MLG to current Workpoint
- turn this product goal/spec into an executable audited graph

NON-TRIGGERS
- implementing one already-designed task
- brainstorming without durable project authority
- replacing Project Genesis, Mission Canvas, Beads, Workpoint, or Trajectory

PHASED WORKFLOW
0. Scope and authority bootstrap: project identity/verify, operator intent, safety/mutation boundary, current Workpoint/Trajectory resume.
1. Scope discovery: canonical repo/worktree, stack, live inventory/data/schema, docs/specs, code/call stacks, tests, external policy, active/closed/deferred task-provider items, and contradictory sources.
2. State and gap evidence: observed current state, desired end state, acceptance/non-done checks, freshness, blockers, anomalies, false-completion risks.
3. Decision closure: LOCKED, EVIDENCE_RESOLVED, OPERATOR_GATE, SUPERSEDED; no silent implementation choices or TBD leakage.
4. Risk/blocker ownership: stable IDs, trigger/impact/gate effect, accountable role, evidence, recovery, review/freshness.
5. Work decomposition: shared foundations, lanes, per-object leaves, milestones, terminal gates, parallelizable versus serial work.
6. Dependency graph design: exact predecessor/successor edges, authority edges, critical path, dynamic dependencies, N-of-M thresholds, rollback/evidence gates, failure propagation.
7. Point-of-need task contracts: purpose, inputs, outputs/consumers, exact files/components, call stack, commands, schemas/migrations, tests, evidence, security/resources, rollback, done/not-done, owner, authority. If exact details depend on research, create an explicit design/research predecessor instead of leaving the implementation task ambiguous.
8. Dry graph validation before mutation: unique nodes, existing refs, topological sort, no missing predecessor, no scope drift, terminal ancestry, authority ancestry, threshold guards.
9. Provider-neutral materialization: preview then create/update tasks through the project task provider (Beads when bound), preserve existing history, label stable graph-node IDs, add blocking/related/parent edges idempotently.
10. Persisted graph audit: reread provider state; prove exact edge parity, zero cycles/orphans, complete contracts, active-task disposition, reachability, critical path, dynamic-slot policy, and impossible false terminal completion.
11. Trajectory extrapolation: preserve HLT; infer evidence-backed MLG, STG, Waypoints, current action, current Workpoint, and next ready frontier from the audited graph; never infer deadlines or authorization.
12. Authorization transition: distinguish READY from AUTHORIZED; record explicit operator receipt before executable descendants; recompute frontier.
13. Evidence/learning/handoff: stable refs, prediction evaluation, metacog lesson, Workpoint + Trajectory checkpoint, bounded next possibility.

CORE TOOL COMPOSITION
- Scope: focusa_project_identity, focusa_project_verify, focusa_project_card.
- Context: focusa_context_cognition, focusa_traverse, focusa_active_object_resolve, repository read/search and live read-only data queries.
- Trajectory: focusa_trajectory_view/history/define_goal/assess/propose_workpoint/checkpoint/resume.
- Design: focusa_call_stack_design/verify, Mission Canvas task-plan primitives where applicable.
- Workpoint: focusa_workpoint_checkpoint/resume/link_evidence.
- Task provider: Project Genesis/provider binding plus br/bd preview/create/update/dep/cycle/ready/sync when Beads is canonical.
- Evidence/learning: focusa_evidence_capture, focusa_predict_record/evaluate/stats, focusa_metacog_retrieve/capture.
- Recovery: focusa_tool_doctor, project verify, state hygiene diagnosis, typed failure receipts.

OUTPUT ARTIFACTS
ScopeDiscoveryPacket; CurrentStateGapAssessment; DecisionClosureRegister; RiskBlockerRegister; ExecutionGraphPlan; PointOfNeedTaskContract set; ProviderMaterializationReceipt; GraphAuditProof; TrajectoryLadder; ReadyFrontier; AuthorizationReceipt requirement; WorkpointResumePacket.

WIRE PITCH DOGFOOD EVIDENCE
The manual workflow produced Specs 03–12, 591 graph nodes, 2,642 blocking edges, 117 research/auth/operational triplets, 117 deferred unique slots for an exact-105 threshold, zero cycles, static 117 terminal ancestry, corrected an inferred push gate, closed planning authority, derived R4 authorization, and opened DES-DATA. This issue should preserve those lessons as the canonical skill eval case.

DUPLICATE REVIEW
Searched all open/closed/deferred Focusa Beads and repo skills for roadmap-to-Workpoint, execution graph, dependency graph, scope discovery, decision closure, point-of-need, graph audit, task graph, and Trajectory ladder. Adjacent but non-duplicate owners: focusa-vbcqu.3.1 Project Genesis first Workpoint; focusa-mc-st2 task-plan graph; focusa-mc-st3 Beads materialization; focusa-9o3v.6 Trajectory derivation; focusa-spec-implementation skill.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Add `.pi/skills/focusa-roadmap-to-workpoint/SKILL.md` plus numbered runbook/reference files with progressive disclosure and bounded core prompt size.
2. Register one clear ownership row in the skill ownership manifest; orchestration must delegate to Project Genesis, Mission Canvas, Spec Implementation, Trajectory, Workpoint, Evidence, Prediction, and provider owners without semantic duplication.
3. Define typed inputs/outputs for every phase and a resumable workflow receipt carrying project_root, continuity_id, task-provider binding, graph digest, Workpoint ID, and Trajectory ID.
4. Implement plan-only and approval-gated materialize modes; default is read-only/preview. No task or state mutation is inferred.
5. Require canonical live authority and freshness evidence; reject static catalog counts or stale cross-project context when live authority conflicts.
6. Require decision closure statuses (LOCKED/EVIDENCE_RESOLVED/OPERATOR_GATE/SUPERSEDED), stable blocker/risk IDs, and no unresolved implementation choice hidden in a task.
7. Require point-of-need task contracts with exact inputs, outputs, consumers, files/components, call stack, commands, tests, rollback, evidence, owner, and authority; unresolved details become explicit predecessor tasks.
8. Support static edges and typed dynamic dependencies/N-of-M thresholds without premature binding; prove uniqueness/cardinality at closure.
9. Materialize idempotently through the bound provider, preserve existing issues/history, map every active item or explicit disposition, and avoid duplicate tasks.
10. Audit the persisted graph independently: exact node/edge parity, zero cycles/orphans, all non-root predecessors, authority ancestry, critical path, terminal ancestry, threshold guards, ready frontier, and false-completion simulation.
11. Derive and persist the MLG → STG → Waypoint → current action → current Workpoint ladder from audited evidence while preserving HLT authority and distinguishing READY from AUTHORIZED.
12. Provide fail-closed recovery for broad cwd, cross-project state bleed, missing writer lease, provider mismatch, stale evidence, partial materialization, and interrupted idempotent reruns.
13. Add behavioral tests using Wire Pitch as an eval fixture: 117 objects, exact-105 dynamic selection, parallel lanes, existing task reuse, operator correction removing an inferred push dependency, and transition from graph acceptance to first design Workpoint.
14. Add smaller fixtures for a finite DAG and an open-ended task stream; prove the skill does not materialize unknown future work prematurely.
15. Document all tools used, why each is selected, authority/side effects, expected receipts, evidence capture, prediction evaluation, metacog lesson, and handoff/checkpoint sequence.
16. Expose the skill through installed/global generation, Agent Card/discovery metadata, docs index, and cross-harness equivalents.
17. End-to-end proof must start from an ambiguous project session and finish with a verified project scope, persisted audited graph, explicit authorization gate, canonical Trajectory ladder, and resumable current Workpoint—without implementation drift.
18. Duplicate audit remains attached; no existing primitive skill is replaced or copied.
19. Include and maintain the complete Tool Routing Matrix from the issue notes: orientation/discovery, project/genesis, context, Trajectory/temporal, design/Workpoint/evidence, provider graph materialization, lineage/recovery, prediction/metacog, autonomous execution, diagnostics/hygiene, resource/token control, UIAI research, security/release/outcome, and local provider/repo proof tools. Each entry states descriptor, when to use it, authority/side-effect boundary, and fallback.
20. Emit a machine-readable `tools_used` receipt containing tool name, descriptor, phase, reason, scope, side_effect, result/evidence ref, and recovery taken; distinguish tools available from tools actually invoked.
21. Add a tool-completeness eval that compares the skill matrix against Agent Card/capability registry and fails when a relevant owned capability is omitted or a retired/unrelated capability is injected.
notes:
Suggested from the 2026-07-29 Wire Pitch roadmap/graph/Trajectory dogfood. Operator requested clear documentation for future agents and explicit recall of the manual steps/tools. This is a skill proposal, not admission to the locked release without separate authority.

TOOL ROUTING MATRIX v1 — all useful tools for the proposed skill

A. ORIENTATION AND PROGRESSIVE DISCOVERY
- focusa_agent_prompt — canonical Pi guidance.
- focusa_utility_card — startup/resume/recovery brevity and scope rules.
- focusa_agent_card — cross-harness interfaces/capability families.
- focusa_tool_search — rank narrow capabilities before schema loading.
- focusa_tool_describe — cold-load one exact tool contract.
- focusa_tool_graph — inspect dependencies/likely-next tools.
- focusa_tool_bundle — bounded family metadata/schema bundle.

B. PROJECT IDENTITY, BOOTSTRAP, AND GENESIS
- focusa_project_identity — resolve typed project/worktree/subpath candidates.
- focusa_project_verify — fail closed on project/root/remote mismatch.
- focusa_project_card — synthesize project intelligence and recommended sequence.
- focusa_project_card_outcome — attach verified outcome and improve project-card learning.
- focusa_project_bootstrap — preview/apply/repair local project discipline with confirmation.
- focusa_project_genesis — HLT-to-first-Workpoint onboarding transaction.
- focusa_hlt_history — recover exact root-goal wording and fallback provenance.
- focusa-agent-bootstrap and focusa-project-scope skills — route initial orientation and cross-project authority.

C. CONTEXT DISCOVERY AND CURATION
- focusa_context_cognition — typed project context packet.
- focusa_context_cognition_render — bounded human-readable packet.
- focusa_context_cognition_proof — proof command bundle.
- focusa_context_cognition_curate — token-budgeted file/doc/evidence selection.
- focusa_context_cognition_curate_eval — precision/recall/F1 eval.
- focusa_context_cognition_curate_optimize — promote/rollback curator artifacts.

title: P0 Pi startup: infer project scope without blocking degraded verification prompt
description:
Observed failure

On macOS startup, Pi proposed `project_root=/Volumes/Macintosh HD/Users/vsmith`, `/project/verify` returned degraded, and the extension opened a modal Yes/No prompt before the agent could use Focusa identity, Workpoint, git, marker, environment, or recovery evidence. This stopped conversation and progress.

Verified design defects

1. `apps/pi-extension/src/session.ts` treats every non-verified `project_verify` result as a startup confirmation event, even when degradation is safely recoverable.
2. The extension already has `queueProjectIdentityBootstrapTurn`, a non-modal agent/tool recovery path, but degraded verify does not route through it.
3. Scope-safety logic is split across TypeScript and Rust and does not consistently reject macOS volume-mounted user homes such as `/Volumes/<volume>/Users/<user>`.
4. A broad cwd-only path is promoted to a project candidate instead of being retained only as an ancestor-search anchor.
5. Verification status is treated as a boolean rather than a capability-bearing authority decision.

Design objective

Pi startup SHALL keep conversation and agent reasoning flowing while Focusa deterministically resolves project authority. It SHALL never weaken `project_root + continuity_id` authority, auto-bind genuine cross-project ambiguity, or allow unverified project-state writes. Operator interruption is a last-resort, mutation-bound decision—not a startup default.

Canonical startup state machine

`COLLECT -> NORMALIZE -> RECONCILE -> VERIFY -> {BOUND | RECOVERING | QUARANTINED}`

1. **COLLECT:** Gather the invocation's explicit project root, cwd, session cwd, git top-level/worktree/common-dir/origin, `.focusa-project.json`, `.git`, `.beads`, workspace markers, active canonical Workpoint scope, continuity ID, persisted last-verified binding, Focusa environment hints, and daemon ProjectIdentity candidates. Record provenance and freshness for every signal.
2. **NORMALIZE:** Canonicalize paths with realpath where possible; compare candidates with canonical `HOME`; recognize `/Users/<user>`, `/home/<user>`, and `/Volumes/<volume>/Users/<user>` as user-home search anchors rather than project roots; preserve worktree root plus canonical parent identity; reject system, temp, agent-runtime, and broad roots. Rust is the canonical ScopeSafety policy. TypeScript uses a versioned parity contract/conformance fixture for offline preflight rather than an independently drifting policy.
3. **RECONCILE:** Score independent evidence, not path-name guesses. Auto-selection requires one strong current signal with no conflicting strong signal, or a corroborated same-project worktree/persisted binding with matching repo/project fingerprint. A persisted root never overrides contradictory current git/marker evidence.
4. **VERIFY:** Call ProjectIdentity first with all bounded candidates and `persisted_project_root`, then `project_verify` only for the selected candidate. Verification returns a typed ProjectBindingDecision, not a boolean.
5. **BOUND:** Verified or same-project worktree-rebound scope is adopted automatically; continuity is preserved; Workpoint, Trajectory, and preload recovery continue; no modal or warning remains.
6. **RECOVERING:** One safe candidate exists but evidence is stale/incomplete or the daemon is temporarily degraded. Continue conversation, reads, planning, and non-project-local reasoning immediately. Fence durable project-state writes. Queue one non-modal ProjectScopeRecoveryPacket for the agent to run `focusa_project_identity -> focusa_project_verify -> focusa_workpoint_resume/checkpoint`. Clear the packet automatically when verification succeeds.
7. **QUARANTINED:** Multiple strong candidates conflict, the only candidate is unsafe, or cross-project continuity disagrees. Continue unbound conversation and diagnostics; do not adopt a root or perform project-state mutation. Ask the operator only when deterministic/tool recovery is exhausted and an actual project-aware mutation is pending. The prompt presents bounded candidates and evidence differences—not Yes/No acceptance of an unsafe path.

Authority and interruption policy

- Startup MUST NOT call `ctx.ui.confirm` for recoverable degraded verification.
- **BOUND:** full scoped capability.
- **RECOVERING:** read, plan, and tool-recovery capability; project writes return a typed `scope_recovery_required` envelope.
- **QUARANTINED:** unbound/read-only capability; cross-project writes fail closed.
- Offline reuse is allowed only for a fresh last-verified binding whose session/repo/worktree fingerprint still matches; otherwise RECOVERING.
- A single bounded widget may show recovery status without stealing editor focus. Repeated notifications, modal loops, and duplicate recovery packets are forbidden.
- Operator input is retained and processed while recovery runs. Recovery cancellation never discards input.

Project Bootstrap and Genesis integration

The binding state machine is the authority gate immediately before Project Bootstrap; it does not replace Bootstrap or Genesis.

1. **BOUND + ready receipt:** Read `/v1/project/bootstrap/status`. If Bootstrap and Genesis receipts are ready, skip onboarding and continue directly from the active Workpoint.
2. **BOUND + existing incomplete project:** Surface the canonical Bootstrap or Genesis `next_action` non-modally. Read, planning, and diagnosis continue. Apply, repair, rollback, takeover, and Genesis commit retain their existing confirmation requirements.
3. **BOUND + explicit new-project intent:** Run Bootstrap preview automatically. Bootstrap apply still requires explicit confirmation; successful apply invokes the existing Genesis chain, which creates the marker, HLT/Trajectory, coordination owner, and first canonical Workpoint.
4. **RECOVERING:** Never bootstrap a merely inferred candidate. Finish identity reconciliation first; conversation and project-neutral planning continue meanwhile.
5. **QUARANTINED:** Never preview or apply Bootstrap against an unresolved root. Candidate choice is deferred until deterministic evidence or mutation-bound operator selection resolves authority.
6. Bootstrap, Genesis, marker, and first-Workpoint receipts become strong evidence for subsequent ProjectBindingDecision reconciliation, eliminating repeated startup onboarding.
7. Existing idempotency and transaction receipts remain authoritative, so reconnects and resumed Pi sessions cannot duplicate Bootstrap or Genesis.

Typed decision receipt

Persist `ProjectBindingDecisionV1` in the session-scoped store with: decision ID, state, selected project/worktree roots, continuity ID, candidate set, evidence sources/freshness, rejection reasons, scope-safety policy version, repo/project fingerprints, confidence, verification status, permitted capability tier, recovery packet ref, operator decision ref if any, effective timestamp, and superseded decision. Re-evaluate only when cwd, git, marker, Workpoint, continuity, or daemon identity changes. Unchanged evidence MUST NOT reprompt.

Call stack

Pi `session_start` -> `resolveStartupProjectBinding` handler -> local EvidenceCollector + canonical ScopeSafety -> ProjectBindingReconciler -> `/project/identity` adapter -> `/project/verify` adapter -> ProjectBindingDecision reducer/store -> Workpoint/Trajectory/preload continuation -> bounded status/advisory output.

Typed design: `019faf65-f17b-7771-88e6-02697f21489b`.

Acceptance and proof

1. macOS E2E starting at `/Volumes/Macintosh HD/Users/vsmith` never promotes the user home and never opens the degraded-verify modal.
2. Starting inside a marked/git project auto-binds and reaches Workpoint recovery without interruption.
3. Starting from a broad home with one persisted same-repo verified project auto-recovers only after fingerprint reconciliation.
4. Stale persisted project versus a different current repo enters QUARANTINED and blocks project writes without blocking chat.
5. Two plausible projects produce one bounded candidate-selection request only at the first pending project mutation.
6. Daemon offline/degraded mode continues non-blocking with the correct capability tier and later converges without duplicate prompts.
7. Same canonical project across worktrees rebinds automatically while preserving worktree identity.
8. Rust/TypeScript scope-safety parity tests cover Linux homes, direct macOS homes, macOS `/Volumes` aliases, broad roots, temp roots, runtime directories, spaces, symlinks, and Unicode.
9. Session lifecycle race tests prove exactly one binding receipt and one recovery packet per evidence revision.
10. Telemetry proves startup latency, automatic resolution rate, operator-interruption rate, false-bind rate, recovery duration, and blocked-write reasons without exposing paths unnecessarily.
11. Mutation tests prove no project-aware durable write occurs in RECOVERING or QUARANTINED state.
12. Existing verified startup, resumed session, worktree rebound, fork/compaction continuation, and unbound-project guidance tests remain green.
13. A ready existing project bypasses Bootstrap and Genesis and resumes its active Workpoint.
14. An incomplete existing project renders the canonical Bootstrap/Genesis next action without a startup modal or duplicate transaction.
15. An explicitly requested greenfield project runs preview first, requires confirmation for apply/commit, then reaches exactly one first Workpoint.
16. RECOVERING and QUARANTINED states prove that Bootstrap apply, repair, rollback, takeover, and Genesis commit cannot execute before binding authority is BOUND.
notes: Implemented at 80f22b51. Typed ProjectBindingDecisionV1, non-modal RECOVERING/QUARANTINED/BOUND startup, fingerprint reconciliation, mutation fence, deduplicated recovery, telemetry, explicit Genesis confirmation. OVH gates PASS; core 8/8; Mac E2E 4/4; evidence docs/evidence/project-binding/focusa-vbcqu.3.4-startup-binding-acceptance.txt.

title: MCP tool layer should match focusa doctor --json surface (single-round-trip 'what is broken')
description:
## Problem

The Focusa MCP tool layer (`focusa_project_identity`, `focusa_tool_doctor`, `focusa_trajectory_view`, etc.) returns **structured records with implicit status**, not error messages with reasons. When an agent or operator asks "what's broken?" or "why is this card `degraded`?", the tool responses are projections that drop the actionable detail the underlying daemon produces.

In contrast, `focusa doctor --json` (the underlying CLI) already returns the full structured report: `status`, `summary`, `next_action`, `why`, `commands`, `recovery`, `details.checks[16]` (with `name`/`status`/`path` per check), `readiness_categories`, `warnings`, `evidence_refs`, and `docs`. The MCP tool layer is a partial projection of this surface, and the projection hides the bits an agent needs to act.

## Reproduction

Run from any project under the Focusa MCP (this is what an agent did in a recent session on `/home/focusadev/perpetua`):

```
$ focusa project_identity
{
  "project": "perpetua",
  "status": "degraded",
  "confidence": "medium",
  "stack": "unknown",
  "workspace": "rust-monorepo",
  "urls": { "local_only": true, "root": "http://localhost:8080" },
  ...
  "degraded": true
}
```

There is **no `degraded_reasons` field.** The reason `status=degraded` is implicit: `stack=unknown` (no manifest), `urls.local_only=true` (no live server), `workspace=rust-monorepo` was operator-supplied, not tool-verified. An agent reading this response cannot tell what to fix first.

Compare with the underlying `focusa doctor --json`:

```
$ focusa doctor --json | jq '.status, .summary, .next_action, .why'
"blocked"
"1 doctor check(s) blocked; readiness categories split runtime/source/release planes"
"Run the recovery command for the first blocked check, then re-run focusa doctor"
"Spec92 requires one agent-first command center covering health, contracts, workpoint/work-loop, telemetry, cache, Pi skills, Mac app, release proof, Guardian, and cleanup readiness."
```

The CLI version returns:
- `status: "blocked"` (specific)
- `summary` (one-sentence explanation)
- `next_action` (the exact command)
- `why` (the Spec92 reason)
- `recovery` (commands to run)
- `details.checks[16]` with `name`/`status`/`path` per check
- `readiness_categories` (split by runtime/source/release plane)
- `warnings`, `evidence_refs`, `docs`

The MCP version returns **none of these.** The agent has to make 4-5 tool calls + a manual synthesis to answer the question the CLI already answers in one.

## Evidence

A recent bootstrap-status workflow on the `perpetua` project (continuous_id `focusa-cont-focusa-53795608-...`) required:

1. `focusa_project_identity` → `status=degraded, confidence=medium`
2. `focusa_project_verify` → `verified=false, status=mismatch, confidence=low`
3. `focusa_tool_doctor` → `workpoint=not_found, work_loop=blocked, recommended=REQUIRED NEXT: run focusa_trajectory_view...`
4. `focusa_trajectory_view` → `current=missing, gap=Trajectory gap unclear until desired end state and current verified state are both present`
5. `focusa_resource_mode` → `mode=normal, within_budget` (the *only* clean card)
6. Manual synthesis by the agent to produce a 1-line answer to the operator's question

The answer could have been: `focusa doctor --json | jq '.status, .details.checks[] | select(.status == "blocked") | .recovery'`. One call.

## Proposed fix

Make the MCP tool layer match the daemon's `focusa doctor --json` surface. Specifically:

### P0 — One-call doctor (matches existing CLI)

Add a `focusa_doctor --detail` MCP tool that returns the same shape as `focusa doctor --json`. Acceptance:

```bash
focusa_doctor --detail
```

Returns a flat array of cards:

```json
{
  "readiness": "blocked",
  "cards": [
    {
      "card": "project_identity",
      "status": "degraded",
      "reason_codes": ["NO_MANIFEST", "NO_LIVE_URL", "OPERATOR_SUPPLIED_HINT"],
      "fix": "Phase 0.5 writes go.mod and svelte/package.json; systemctl starts the server."
    },
    {
      "card": "workpoint",
      "status": "blocked",
      "reason_codes": ["WORKPOINT_NOT_FOUND"],
      "fix": "focusa_workpoint_checkpoint --project-root <root> --mission <m> --next <n>"
    }
  ],
  "recommended_next": "focusa_trajectory_observe --auto"
}
```

### P0 — Explicit `degraded_reasons` per card

Each MCP tool that returns `degraded` (or any non-`ok` status) must include a `degraded_reasons: [...]` array. Each reason is a typed code with a `fix` string. The agent reads the codes, looks up the fix, applies it, re-runs the tool.

### P1 — `focusa_trajectory_observe --auto`

The trajectory card returns `current=missing` because no `observed_state` has been asserted. The tool should accept a verb that derives `observed_state` from the project (last commit, doc count, manifest presence, server health) without requiring the agent to write a sentence. Acceptance: `focusa_trajectory_observe --auto` fills `observed_state` automatically and re-runs `trajectory_assess`.

### P1 — `focusa_project_verify` returns the relationship

`status=mismatch` is currently a black box. The tool should return `saved_scope`, `current_scope`, and `relationship` (`informational` / `blocking` / `supersession`) so the agent knows what to do.

### P2 — Workpoint `next` re-validates against live state

Workpoints with `partial handoff` re-validate their `next` field against the live state. If the action has been completed, surface: `"next action satisfied; suggest re-targeting"`.

## Why this matters

The Focusa doc inventory already establishes the principle: **"agent's first move on any app error is to read the logs"** (Spec 102 / Spec 92 / Spec 105). The tool layer that delivers logs to the agent must be a single round-trip, not a multi-call synthesis.

Currently, asking "what's broken?" via the MCP tool layer is a 5-call exercise. Asking the same question via `focusa doctor --json` is a 1-call exercise. The MCP layer is a partial projection that drops the actionable detail. The fix is to make the projection match the source.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `focusa_doctor --detail` (or equivalent) returns a flat array of cards with `card`, `status`, `reason_codes`, and `fix` per card.
2. Every MCP tool that returns a non-`ok` status includes an explicit `degraded_reasons` (or equivalent) array.
3. `focusa_trajectory_observe --auto` works without requiring the agent to write a sentence.
4. `focusa project_identity --json` includes the same `degraded_reasons` array as `focusa doctor --json` surfaces.
5. The "what's broken?" question is answerable in 1 round-trip via the MCP tool layer, matching the existing `focusa doctor --json` capability.

## Related

- Spec 92: agent-first polish hooks
- Spec 102: agent UX composition and real-life test
- Spec 105: agent DX / UX merged scope
- Spec 89: focusa tool suite improvement and hardening
- `/v1/doctor` API route (already exposes `api_cli_parity` block — the projection gap is the issue)

## Labels

`agent-dx`, `tool-surface`, `mcp-layer`, `P1`
